newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil to stop gas flaring at Heidrun.
newsitem.headline: Statoil to stop gas flaring at Heidrun.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Thursday it would stop flaring gas at the Heidrun field in the Norwegian Sea.
The gas will be reinjected into the reservoir for later sale, cutting emissions of carbon dioxide by about 13,500 tonnes per year, the company's Status Weekly newsletter said.

Statoil said it was using the same ignition system technology used to eliminate flaring at the North Sea Gullfaks A and C installations. The flare will only be lit in the event of process irregularities.

The modification work cost around 38 million crowns but will reduce the company's liability to Norway's carbon tax. The pilot flame consumes about six million cubic metres of gas per year and the tax is levied at 0.85 crown per cubic metre of gas flared.
